description.narrative: 1. Workers' Organisations have increased effective representation of workers for which home is the workplace to ensure that regulations and policies are formulated through inclusive social dialogue, including collective agreements established with employers and their organizations; (increase in union membership of HBWs, trained and also included in the leadership role). 2. WOs have implemented campaigns to improve compliance with a law, policy or regulation to improve worker protection; (formation of national working group on homebased and informal workers, running joint advocacy and action, including on drafting national policy, inclusion in social security and social protection, and effective implementation of labour law, with special focus on piece rate wages and OSH). 3. WOs have expanded services that effectively facilitate transitions to formality or improve the protection of domestic workers and other groups for which home is the workplace. (piece rate wages – maintaining wage records and negotiation of wages, safe and healthy home as a workplace, financial literacy training for homebased workers, business literacy training for collectives of workers, or workers who want to become micro entrepreneurs, participatory appraisal and evidence collection for identifying and unionizing workers, enabling access to government schemes and services, and informed advocacy and action). 1.Developed Participatory Approasal (PA) tool for the use by WOs in order to identify and unionize invisible wokers; through leadership training, contributed to build the leadership skills among members of home workers groups and associations, with special focus on women members through the ILO/JPN project "Towards Fair and Sustainable Global Supply Chains: Promoting rights of invisible workers in South Asia" (SGSCs) . 2.Strengthened advocacy for a policy framework on home workers; organised policy dialogues on the feasibility of social protection extension to informal workers, especially the homeworkers; provided technical inputs on the drafting process of national policy framework for homeworkers. 3.Provided training to tripartite plus partners on wage setting and wage negotiation; developed training materials, handbooks and videos on safety and health at workplaces, developed literacy manuals and developed trainers through training f trainers, developed handbook on labour laws and provisions with government schemes in order to enhance awareness campaigns of unions and employer's associations about labour laws and other government provisions from the SGSCs Project (RAS/17/06/JPN)
